title: [C13T2] - Owned and rented accommodation in England and Wales
prompt: The chart below shows the percentage of households in owned and rented accommodation in England and Wales between 1918 and 2011. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the proportion of households owning and renting their homes in England and Wales between 1918 and 2011.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the two categories displayed opposite trends throughout the period, with home ownership gradually becoming more popular while rented housing showed a corresponding decline. Additionally, rental properties dominated in the early years, whereas properties owned by occupants became more prevalent from 1971 onwards.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at households renting their homes, in 1918, 77% of households were tenants, representing the vast majority. This figure subsequently decreased steadily to 69% in both 1939 and 1953, before continuing its downward trajectory to 59% in 1961 and 50% in 1971. Following this, the proportion of rental accommodation declined further to 41% in 1981 and then dropped to 31% by 1991. It eventually hit its lowest point at 30% in 2001, after which rented properties saw a slight recovery to 35% in 2011.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Conversely, home ownership started at just 23% in 1918. The percentage initially rose to 31% by 1939 and maintained this level in 1953, before increasing to 41% in 1961. By 1971, homeownership reached 50%, marking the point where it equaled renting. This upward trend persisted throughout the following decades, with properties owned by occupants climbing to 59% in 1981 and 69% in 1991, ultimately peaking at 70% in 2001, though this figure subsequently fell back to 65% by the end of the period.
